LO-1.learner_does: Divides a whole number of up to four digits by 10 by shifting every digit one place to the right, producing the correct quotient.

LO-2.learner_does: Divides a whole number of up to four digits by 100 by shifting every digit two places to the right, producing the correct quotient.

LO-3.learner_does: Explains why the place-value shift is the reliable rule for dividing by 10 or 100, and why crossing off a zero is not.

scenes.narration_text: Today we are looking at what happens to a whole number when you divide it by 10, and then by 100.
scenes.visual_description: A presenter standing in front of a clean, empty whiteboard, with a friendly smile and a marker in hand.
scenes.media_rationale: Human or social moment: the welcome.

source_refs.quote: Today we are looking at what happens to a whole number when you divide it by 10, and then by 100.

scenes.narration_text: Every whole number is built out of place value columns. From the right, we have ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands.
scenes.visual_description: A diagram showing the place value columns, with labels and arrows to illustrate the concept.

source_refs.quote: Every whole number is built out of place value columns. From the right, we have ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands.

scenes.narration_text: Dividing by 10 makes a number ten times smaller. When a number gets ten times smaller, every digit in it moves one place to the right.
scenes.visual_description: An animation showing a number being divided by 10, with the digits moving one place to the right.
scenes.media_rationale: The step is a transformation carried by a person: the presenter explains and demonstrates the concept.

source_refs.quote: Dividing by 10 makes a number ten times smaller. When a number gets ten times smaller, every digit in it moves one place to the right.

scenes.narration_text: For a whole number that ends in a zero, that zero moves off the end and disappears, because there is nothing to the right of the ones column for it to move into.
scenes.visual_description: An example of a number ending in a zero, with the zero moving off the end and disappearing.
scenes.media_rationale: The step is a numeric transformation: the zero moves off the end and disappears.

source_refs.quote: For a whole number that ends in a zero, that zero moves off the end and disappears, because there is nothing to the right of the ones column for it to move into.

scenes.narration_text: Dividing by 100 makes a number one hundred times smaller. One hundred is ten times ten. So dividing by 100 is the same as dividing by 10, and then dividing by 10 again.
scenes.visual_description: A diagram showing the relationship between dividing by 10 and dividing by 100.
scenes.media_rationale: Static concept: the relationship between dividing by 10 and dividing by 100.

source_refs.quote: Dividing by 100 makes a number one hundred times smaller. One hundred is ten times ten. So dividing by 100 is the same as dividing by 10, and then dividing by 10 again.

scenes.narration_text: That means every digit moves two places to the right instead of one. A number with two zeros on the end loses both of them.
scenes.visual_description: An example of a number with two zeros on the end, with the zeros moving off the end and disappearing.
scenes.media_rationale: The step is a numeric transformation: the zeros move off the end and disappear.

source_refs.quote: That means every digit moves two places to the right instead of one. A number with two zeros on the end loses both of them.

scenes.narration_text: It helps to know why this works rather than only that it works. A digit in the tens column is worth ten times what the same digit is worth in the ones column.
scenes.visual_description: A diagram showing the place value of digits in different columns.
scenes.media_rationale: Static concept: the place value of digits in different columns.

source_refs.quote: It helps to know why this works rather than only that it works. A digit in the tens column is worth ten times what the same digit is worth in the ones column.

scenes.narration_text: So moving a digit one column to the right divides what it is worth by exactly ten. Doing that to every digit at once divides the whole number by ten.
scenes.visual_description: An animation showing a number being divided by 10, with the digits moving one place to the right and the place value changing.
scenes.media_rationale: The step is a transformation carried by a person: the presenter explains and demonstrates the concept.

source_refs.quote: So moving a digit one column to the right divides what it is worth by exactly ten. Doing that to every digit at once divides the whole number by ten.

scenes.narration_text: People often say 'dividing by 10 means crossing off a zero.' That works for whole numbers that end in a zero and it fails for every other number, because there is no zero to cross off.
scenes.visual_description: An example of a number that does not end in a zero, with an attempt to cross off a zero and an explanation of why it fails.
scenes.media_rationale: The step is a numeric transformation: the attempt to cross off a zero fails.

source_refs.quote: People often say 'dividing by 10 means crossing off a zero.' That works for whole numbers that end in a zero and it fails for every other number, because there is no zero to cross off.

scenes.narration_text: The reliable version is the one about columns: every digit shifts one place right for each ten you divide by.
scenes.visual_description: A summary diagram showing the place value columns and the effect of dividing by 10 or 100.
scenes.media_rationale: Static concept: the summary of the place value columns and the effect of dividing by 10 or 100.

source_refs.quote: The reliable version is the one about columns: every digit shifts one place right for each ten you divide by.

design_notes: The lesson starts with an introduction to the concept of dividing by 10 and 100, followed by a series of scenes that explain and demonstrate the concept. The learner is then given the opportunity to practice dividing by 10 and 100, and to explain the reliable rule. The lesson ends with a summary diagram that reinforces the key concepts.
